newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Moscow mayor says Russia should let Cechnya go.
newsitem.headline: Moscow mayor says Russia should let Cechnya go.

text.p: Moscow Mayor Yuri Luzhkov, in a diversion from Kremlin policy, said in a newspaper interview published on Thursday that Russia should let Chechnya break away and draw up formal borders with the rebel region.

"You cannot force someone else to love you," Luzhkov told Trud newspaper in an interview printed one day after Chechnya swore in a new president following a 21-month conflict with Russian troops over its independence demands.
"Russia should let Chechnya go... We have to demarcate the border, sign all the necessary agreements and regulate entry and exit between Russia and Chechnya."

Russia, fearing Chechen secession could foment separatism elsewhere in the vast country, says the region cannot be formally allowed to break away and hopes economic inducements will dissuade it from doing so.
Foreign governments, unwilling to anger the Kremlin, have refrained from recognising Chechnya's independence.
"Chechnya will seek full independence before 2000 anyway. It will never be a disciplined part of the federation again," said Luzhkov, who is a political ally of President Boris Yeltsin.
He said the much-discussed option of making Chechnya a free economic zone was not a solution.
Luzhkov, a potential presidential candidate when Yeltsin leaves office, has increasingly often been expressing views on issues beyond his political jurisdiction.
He said the interests of Russian cossacks living in Chechnya should be respected. The cossacks are leaving in droves, fearing there is no place for them in the mainly Moslem region.
